channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan National Bank Plans Significant Financial Support for Economy and Entrepreneurship
item.description: Uzbekistan's National Bank plans to allocate 38.5 trillion soums in loans this year, supporting economic sectors and entrepreneurship. The bank has already directed 15 trillion soums to key industries and 1.7 trillion to construction projects. Special focus is on youth entrepreneurship, aiming to create jobs for 10,000 more young people.

item.title: 75 kg of Meat Contaminated with Dangerous Bacteria Destroyed in North Kazakhstan
item.description: Seventy-five kilograms of frozen meat found to be contaminated with Listeria monocytogenes bacteria have been destroyed by burning in the North Kazakhstan region. The violation was detected during a market monitoring project. The Ministry of Trade and Integration emphasized the responsibility of entrepreneurs for product safety.

item.title: Fergana Region's Economic Development and Income Growth Priorities Identified
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev chaired a meeting on enhancing reforms, accelerating industrial development, and increasing incomes in the Fergana region. The region expects 9.6% GDP growth, 8.5% industrial growth, and 16.3% service sector growth this year. Discussions focused on untapped potential and new investment projects in energy, construction materials, electrical engineering, and pharmaceuticals.

item.title: Prospects for Cooperation Between Central Asia and Europe Outlined at Berlin Conference
item.description: Eldor Aripov, Director of the Institute for Strategic and Regional Studies of Uzbekistan, participated in the Berlin Conference 2026, discussing strategic autonomy for Europe. He highlighted the improved atmosphere of trust and good neighborliness in Central Asia, driven by Uzbekistan's policies, and outlined approaches for dialogue between Central Asia and European states.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Chamber of Accounts May Audit World Bank Projects
item.description: Uzbekistan's Chamber of Accounts met with World Bank representatives to discuss improving its operations and adopting international audit standards. The Chamber, transitioning to international standards, has gained authority to audit projects funded by international financial institutions. The World Bank positively assessed the first audit of the "EduImkon" program.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Urges Training Villagers to Earn Income Online
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev of Kazakhstan has called for reducing the digital divide and training rural residents to earn income online. He stated that with proper internet access and skills, villagers can become financially independent. Tokayev referred to this as the 'people's digital economy'.

item.title: Uzbekistan Discusses Priorities for Tourism Potential and Cultural Heritage Preservation
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed a presentation on tourism development and future priorities, focusing on major projects in Bukhara. Tasks were set for restoring cultural heritage sites, preserving the historical city's character, and enhancing tourist appeal, including plans for the Ark museum-reserve and Samanid Park.

item.title: UN Special Rapporteur Urges Justice and Support for Afghan Survivors of Violence
item.description: Richard Bennett, the UN Special Rapporteur on human rights in Afghanistan, called for justice and support for survivors of violence on the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women. He emphasized the importance of the 16 Days of Activism campaign for ending impunity and supporting Afghan women and girls' right to live free from gender-based violence.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Ancient Cities May Become Hollywood Film Locations
item.description: Hollywood producer Larry Kasanoff suggested that Samarkand, Bukhara, and Khiva could serve as filming locations for Hollywood movies. A memorandum of cooperation in cinema and tourism was signed, aiming to promote Uzbekistan's heritage and natural potential for international film productions, including a potential adventure blockbuster.

item.title: Taliban Plan to Convert Mullah Mohammad Omar's Zabul Residence into Museum
item.description: Local sources report the Taliban intend to transform Mullah Mohammad Omar's former residence in Zabul Province into a museum. A delegation from the Ministry of Information and Culture has visited the site for preliminary assessments. Millions have reportedly been spent on renovating Omar's grave.

item.title: Pakistan and Netherlands Discuss Militant Groups' Presence in Afghanistan
item.description: Pakistan's special representative for Afghanistan, Mohammad Sadiq Khan, met with Dutch officials in Islamabad to discuss regional security and the presence of militant groups in Afghanistan. They referenced UN reports and Kabul's rejection of such allegations.

item.title: Tokayev and Putin Meet Young AI Talents at Conference
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Russia's President Vladimir Putin met with young participants at the AI Journey 2026 conference. Tokayev congratulated the AI Olympiad winners, emphasizing the elder generation's role in creating conditions for their professional growth, which is of state importance for economic development and security.

item.title: Tokayev and Putin Discuss Future of AI with Students and Schoolchildren
item.description: Presidents Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Vladimir Putin discussed the future of artificial intelligence with students and schoolchildren from Kazakhstan, Russia, and India. The meeting, held at the AI Journey 2026 conference, focused on how AI will transform science, medicine, education, economy, and art. Tokayev emphasized the importance of professional growth for young talent and continued digital transformation.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev proposes joint AI projects for schoolchildren with Russia
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has proposed launching joint educational projects with Russia focused on artificial intelligence for schoolchildren and educators. Speaking at the AI Journey 2026 conference in Moscow, he emphasized the importance of teaching critical thinking and analytical skills amidst AI's rapid information processing capabilities. The initiative aims to foster responsible AI use.

item.title: Trump and NATO Secretary-General Discuss Ukraine War, Iran Conflicts, and Defense Spending
item.description: US President Donald Trump met with NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte to discuss the war in Ukraine, conflicts involving Iran, and increased defense spending by NATO members. Trump described the meeting as highly successful and impactful, emphasizing the need for a peaceful resolution to the Ukraine conflict.

item.title: Bishkek Investment Forum Aims to Become Year-Round Platform, Discusses China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan Railway
item.description: The Bishkek Investment Forum (BIF) aims to transform into a year-round investment platform with an online portal and an "Invest Club." This year's forum attracted over a thousand business representatives and investors. A key discussion point was the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway project and its potential benefits for small and medium-sized businesses.

item.title: UN Experts Urge Inclusive Justice and Rights Guarantees for Afghan Victims
item.description: UN experts emphasize the need for inclusive and comprehensive justice for victims of crimes in Afghanistan, ensuring their rights to truth, justice, and reparation. Efforts to achieve justice for persecution of women and girls must align with addressing other serious crimes. Victims' courage should not be met with abandonment, and clear information must be provided.

item.title: Ashgabat Hosts International Forum on CIS Transport Cooperation and Labor Regulation
item.description: An international forum on "Opportunities for Developing the Organization and Regulation of Labor in Strengthening Transport Links of CIS Member States" was held in Ashgabat. Representatives from various CIS countries discussed enhancing transport cooperation and labor standards within the Commonwealth.

item.title: Two Italian Technicians Killed in Kuwait Drone Attack
item.description: Two Italian technicians working for Rheinmetall died after an Iranian drone attack targeted a military facility in Kuwait. The attack injured four people, with shrapnel causing material damage. Italy's Foreign Ministry confirmed the deaths of the civilian technicians.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Addresses AI Journey 2026 Conference
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev spoke at the AI Journey 2026 International Conference, thanking Russia for its invitation and acknowledging its scientific achievements. He highlighted Russia's historical contributions to science and engineering, noting its current standing in intellectual property applications.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Praises Russian Scientific Achievements at AI Conference
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, speaking at the AI Journey 2026 international conference, thanked Russian President Vladimir Putin for the invitation. He acknowledged Russia's historical scientific contributions and noted its current achievements in technology, citing its second-place ranking in patent applications for unique designs and models.

item.title: Taliban Minister Meets UN Envoy to Discuss Fourth Doha Process Meeting
item.description: Afghanistan's Minister of Industry and Trade, Nooruddin Azizi, met with Rabab Fatima, the UN Secretary-General's Special Representative and Head of UNAMA, to discuss the upcoming fourth Doha Process meeting. They exchanged views on the meeting's objectives, agenda, and organization. The third meeting excluded Afghan women and civil society representatives, drawing criticism.

item.title: Fergana Valley Forms Investment Portfolio of at Least $20 Billion, Establishes Special Industrial Zones
item.description: The Fergana region has formed an investment project portfolio valued at a minimum of $20 billion. A proposal to establish special industrial zones across three districts, covering nearly 1,500 hectares, has been approved. The region plans to attract $6.1 billion in foreign investment by 2027.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Pay Up to $38,000 for Reporting Corruption by 2026
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to offer rewards of up to 17.3 million tenge (approximately $38,000) for reporting corruption offenses by 2026. The Anti-Corruption Agency stated that reward amounts will vary based on the severity of the offense, with larger sums for reporting serious crimes or significant bribery cases. The maximum payout is capped at 4,000 times the monthly calculation index.

item.title: Nearly 58,000 Foreign Nationals Came to Study in Uzbekistan This Year
item.description: Since the beginning of the year, almost 58,000 foreign citizens have come to Uzbekistan for educational purposes, a 1.7-fold increase compared to last year. Turkmenistan and India lead in student numbers, with significant contributions from Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, and China.

item.title: UN Experts Urge Reversal of ICC Decision to Halt Afghanistan Crimes Investigation
item.description: United Nations experts have warned that the International Criminal Court's decision to end its investigation into crimes in Afghanistan will deny justice to victims. They expressed deep concern, calling the halt a blow to the fight against impunity and urging its reversal.

item.title: Taliban Fighter Killed in Clashes With Pakistani Forces in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
item.description: A Taliban fighter, identified as Qari Khairullah, was killed in clashes with Pakistani forces in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. Local sources in Khost reported the incident, stating the fighter had been operating with the Pakistani Taliban against Pakistani forces. His funeral prayer was held in Khost province.

item.title: France Reviews Humanitarian Visa Appeal by 120 Afghan Women
item.description: France's Interior Ministry has referred an appeal from 120 Afghan women seeking increased humanitarian visa allocations and faster processing to the immigration directorate. The women requested protection due to threats in Afghanistan, Iran, and Pakistan. The ministry stated the referral does not guarantee visa approval.

item.title: Uzbekistan Expands Middle East Partnerships for Economic Diversification
item.description: Uzbekistan is actively broadening its partnerships in the Middle East, with President Mirziyoyev recently visiting Jordan and Oman, elevating relations to strategic partnership levels. Experts believe this move diversifies Uzbekistan's foreign economic ties, attracting investment and expanding trade routes and markets.

item.title: Chechen Activist Destroys Surveillance Camera in Kazakhstan Pre-trial Detention
item.description: Chechen activist Mansur Movlayev, held in pre-trial detention in Almaty, reportedly destroyed a surveillance camera in the detention center. His support page and human rights media reported a criminal case has been opened against him for property damage. His lawyer confirmed the camera destruction but was unaware of the criminal case.

item.title: NATO Prepares to Defend Against Russian Nuclear Space Threat
item.description: NATO is preparing to defend itself against a potential Russian nuclear weapon in space, according to German media reports. NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg stated the alliance will protect its security in space. Such a weapon could disable thousands of satellites in orbit.

item.title: Kazakhstan Changes Procedure for Issuing IIN to Foreigners
item.description: Kazakhstan is set to change the procedure for issuing Individual Identification Numbers (IIN) to foreigners. The Ministry of Internal Affairs has approved a new order detailing the updated rules for temporary foreign residents and stateless persons. The changes aim to streamline the process.

item.title: Woman beaten in Shu dies in hospital; suspect arrested
item.description: A woman who was severely beaten in Shu has died from her injuries in the hospital. Police have opened a criminal case, and a 40-year-old suspect has been detained. The woman was reportedly attacked by her former partner on November 23 and brought to the hospital in a coma ten hours later. The 'Nemolchi.kz' foundation confirmed her death.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Launches Online Citizen Reception for Judicial System
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's judicial system has introduced an online reception for citizens, allowing individuals unable to travel to Bishkek to connect with judicial leadership remotely. This initiative aims to improve access to justice and streamline the handling of citizen complaints. The Supreme Court conducted its first online reception with a resident from Osh, who complained about a lengthy case.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans $20 Billion Investment for Fergana Region Development
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev outlined plans to double the income of 1.1 million Fergana region residents by 2027 through industrial, trade, service, and agricultural processing development. The region aims to attract $6.1 billion in foreign investment next year, with a total project portfolio of at least $20 billion, including special industrial zones and manufacturing of electric buses and microchips.

item.title: Young Man's Bullet-Riddled Body Found in Kabul After 25 Days Missing
item.description: The body of Mohammad Omar, a young man from Panjshir Province, was returned to his family in Kabul after being missing for 25 days. He disappeared while traveling from Panjshir to Kabul to renew his driving license. His body, found with multiple bullet wounds, was handed over from a Kabul hospital. Recent incidents raise security concerns.

item.title: Kazakhstan advocates for human control over artificial intelligence in military
item.description: Kazakhstan has called for a ban on fully autonomous lethal weapons systems and stressed the importance of human control over AI in warfare. Speaking at the UN Security Council, the delegation supported legally binding international restrictions on autonomous weapons and urged adherence to international humanitarian law.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan sign roadmap for parliamentary cooperation until 2028
item.description: Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan have signed a roadmap for parliamentary cooperation covering 2027–2028. The agreement was reached during the Second Azerbaijan-Uzbekistan Parliamentary Forum held in Baku, where further expansion of bilateral cooperation was discussed.

item.title: Malaysia Demands $146 Million from Google Over YouTube Content
item.description: Malaysia's communications commission has filed two lawsuits against Google, seeking approximately $146 million in compensation. The regulator accuses Google of failing to effectively combat harmful content on YouTube, including illegal gambling and fraud. The suits cite numerous complaints about content, some of which remained unaddressed for months.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Russia Discuss Developing Digital Transport Corridors and Freight
item.description: Kazakhstan and Russia held talks in Moscow on November 26 to discuss the development of transport corridors, roads, and the implementation of digital technologies in freight transportation. Discussions included routes within the Eurasian Economic Union and the North-South international corridor. Both nations confirmed their interest in further enhancing transport cooperation.
